body.en: Centralisation and decentralisation must be balanced. Scalar chain is the formal line of authority from top to bottom. Order: a place for everything and everyone. Equity: kindliness and justice. Stability of personnel: low labour turnover. Initiative: freedom to think and execute plans. Esprit de corps: team spirit.

title.en: On the board: scalar chain and gang plank

narration.en: Watch the board as we build this up step by step.

say.en: A is the top manager. Authority flows down two chains: B to E, and L to O.
Left chain: B, C, D, E. Right chain: L, M, N, O.
Normally a message from E must go up through D, C and B to A, and then down through L, M and N to O. That is slow in an emergency.
The gang plank lets E talk directly to O, keeping their superiors informed.
Use it only in emergencies; otherwise follow the chain.

explanation.en: Fayol's later principles balance authority, keep the chain of command, and build order, fairness, stability, initiative and team spirit.

right.en: Branch heads approve small loans; big ones go to head office
A clerk's request passes up through the formal line of authority
Every tool has a fixed place, and every worker a fixed job
All workers are treated with kindness and justice, whatever their caste or religion
Staff are not shifted every few months, so turnover stays low
Workers are encouraged to suggest and carry out improvements
The manager says "we", not "I", and builds team spirit

body.en: Fayol looked from top management and gave a general theory of administration based on his personal experience; he insisted on unity of command. Taylor looked from the shop floor, used observation and experiment, aimed at higher productivity, and his functional foremanship ignored unity of command.

points.en: Perspective: top management vs shop floor
Unity of command: followed vs not followed
Basis: personal experience vs observation and experiment

problem.en: In a Belagavi sugar factory, a new manager praises only his relatives, while the old manager used to say "we did it" after every good season. Which two principles are shown by the two managers?

steps.en: Favouring relatives is unfair treatment: it violates equity.
Saying "we did it" builds team spirit: it follows esprit de corps.
Equity also keeps good workers from leaving, supporting stability of personnel.

answer.en: The new manager violates equity; the old manager followed esprit de corps.
